title: elastic-wait-slope-scheduler-with-proactive-kv-hinting
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: In high-concurrency continuous-batching workloads we observed head-of-line effects where a small number of long KV-miss-heavy requests cause repeated batch hold-ups and elevated p99. Motivation: Provide a scheduler heuristic that favors low-wait-slope requests (likely short or cache-hit dominated) to reduce p99 tail while ensuring starvation-free progress for heavy requests. Design: Introduce an 'elastic wait-slope' metric computed per request as recent wait-time divided by estimated service tokens; the admission controller prefers requests with low wait-slope but maintains a dynamically-sized 'elastic window' that guarantees periodic admission of higher-slope requests. To prevent livelock we add a per-queue aging credit that increases admission priority linearly with time and is bounded by the window manager. KV cache integration: A lightweight prefetch hinter predicts likely KV cache misses from tokenized embeddings and request signatures and emits async prefetch requests to the KV layer; the scheduler consults a per-request kv_hint flag to bias admission and to pre-warm KV entries when possible. Timeouts & backoff: Implemented jittered soft-timeouts for queued requests and exponential backoff for repeated prefetch attempts to avoid thundering prefetch storms. Implementation notes: New modules: src/scheduler/wait_slope.rs (heuristic + admission), src/scheduler/window_manager.rs (elastic window logic), src/kv/prefetch_hint.rs (prediction + prefetch pipeline), small integration hooks in src/serve/integration.rs. Exposed runtime knobs in deploy/config/defaults.yaml and an ops page docs/ops/scheduler_tuning.md. Benchmarks: microbench harness (tests/perf/scheduler_bench.rs) shows 8-12% improvement in p99 latency under mixed KV-hit:miss workloads and ~4% average latency improvement; CPU usage increases by ~3-6% depending on workload due to prefetch overhead. Testing: unit and integration tests added; perf harness committed. Rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag scheduler.elastic_wait_slope and kv.prefetch.enabled; staged rollout via canary group then global. Risks: prefetch can increase load on KV; defaults are conservative. Migration: none required. Related: ENG-8124 implements metrics to detect prefetch overload; ENG-8201 ties this work to per-tenant QoS controls.

implement elastic window manager with safety bounds
integration: hook prefetch into scheduler admission path
bench: microbench harness and cfg toggles
docs: operator guide and config knobs
fix: race in window resize under heavy concurrency
review_comments: Luis Ortega: Can you explain how the elastic window size adapts under sustained load? I saw an earlier draft where the window oscillated and caused priority inversion.

Maya Chen: The window manager uses occupancy + recent dequeue rate to grow/shrink with hysteresis and a min-reserve so oscillation amplitude is bounded. Added tests that simulate step-load changes to validate stability.
Priya Natarajan: Prefetch hint looks promising but how do we ensure KV backend isn't overwhelmed?

Maya Chen: Added conservative defaults (max inflight prefetch per-queue, exponential backoff, and operator gauge) and a metric prefetch_overrun. Also made kv.prefetch.enabled=false by default for on-prem installs.
Ethan Park: Need a metric that shows if heavy requests are being starved. Request: add request_age_histogram and admitted_vs_aged counter.
Maya Chen: Added request_age_histogram, admitted_vs_aged counter, and a linear aging credit to the admission logic. Updated docs with guidance on thresholds.
Luis Ortega: CI flake on perf harness reprobed; re-ran bench job and fixed timeout in test fixture. Approve after green.
Priya Natarajan: Approve after addressing comments.
release_notes: Introduce elastic-wait-slope scheduler heuristic to reduce p99 for mixed KV workloads
Add conservative KV prefetch hints to reduce cache-miss latency (disabled by default)
Expose runtime knobs: scheduler.elastic_wait_slope, scheduler.elastic_window_min/max, kv.prefetch.enabled, kv.prefetch.max_inflight
notes_on_performance: Microbench on c6gpu-equivalent nodes: p99 reduced by 8-12% in mixed workloads, p50 improved ~4%; CPU overhead +3-6% depending on prefetch rate. Bench config included in tests/perf/scheduler_bench.rs.
rollout_plan: Feature gated; enable on 5% canary for 24h; monitor request_age_histogram, prefetch_overrun, CPU and KV tail latencies; then 25% for 72h before full rollout.
